title: THE GREATEST LIE (2026) | OFFICIAL SHORT FILM

segments.text: Hundreds of years ago, every  person on the planet could read. And then slowly people stopped and we forgot how important it was. People would have ideas and they would write books and then  those books would change people.

The world was full of words. You didn't have to hide them like we do. Some  people don't want you to learn how to read. I'm sorry for that. I'm still going to teach you and you're going to learn. Did you know mommy's writing a book?

One day you're going to read it  and I hope it changes your world. RADIO: Compliance personnel recovered what the office of  communication access described as a significant   cache of unlicensed printed materials. Residents

reminded, if you become aware... George? "Not a famine of food or a thirst for water, but  a famine of hearing the words." Amos 8:11. There are very few manuscripts  worth dying for. Men die. Their words live on.

At 4:05, one of my runners will create a  disturbance. The front guards will see to it,   allowing you to bypass the entrance. We'll  try to clear the way for you from there. Next,   you'll have to find the manuscript.

Forward. There have been many great lies  told over the course of human history.   Perhaps the greatest lie we told ourselves was  this. That we no longer need to care, to care,

to read, to write, to know, to care to live. So to  understand this story reader, you have work to do. Do you know who wrote that? Very smart, very brave woman. And guess what? What? You were just like her.
